mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a liquid?
mcqs.explanation: Water is a liquid at room temperature, taking the shape of its container while retaining a definite volume. Ice is a solid, sugar is a solid, and air is a gas.

mcqs.question: A student fills a 250 mL beaker with juice and then pours it into a bottle of a different shape. Which statement best describes the volume of the juice after the transfer?

options.A: The volume changes to fit the new container
options.C: The volume becomes larger because the bottle is bigger
options.D: The volume becomes smaller because the bottle is smaller

mcqs.explanation: Liquids have a definite volume; they occupy the same amount of space regardless of the shape of the container that holds them. Only the shape changes, not the volume.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about liquids is a common misconception?

options.A: Liquids take the shape of their container

mcqs.explanation: Liquids do not have a fixed shape; they adapt to the shape of the container they occupy. The other statements correctly describe liquid properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Taking the shape of a container
mcqs.question: Why does water poured into a glass take the shape of the glass?

options.A: Because water molecules are tightly packed and cannot move
options.B: Because water molecules are attracted to the glass walls and spread out
options.C: Because water has no fixed shape and its molecules can move past each other
options.D: Because water expands to fill any space

mcqs.answer: Because water has no fixed shape and its molecules can move past each other
mcqs.explanation: Liquids lack a fixed shape; their molecules are free to slide past one another, allowing the liquid to conform to the shape of its container. Options A and D describe solids, while B is not the primary reason.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the ability to flow of liquids and solids?

options.A: Both liquids and solids flow equally well
options.B: Solids flow more easily than liquids
options.C: Liquids flow while solids retain their shape unless broken
options.D: Neither liquids nor solids can flow

mcqs.answer: Liquids flow while solids retain their shape unless broken
mcqs.explanation: Liquids can flow because their particles can move past each other, whereas solids keep a fixed shape and only change shape when a force breaks them. Options A, B, and D are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: In a science competition, students must select all items that are liquids at room temperature. Which set is correct?
mcqs.explanation: Milk, gasoline, and mercury are all liquids at typical room temperature. Ice is solid, steam is gas, sand is solid, and the gases listed are not liquids.

mcqs.question: What does the term "definite volume" mean for a liquid?

options.A: It can change its volume depending on the container
options.B: It always occupies the same amount of space regardless of the container

mcqs.answer: It always occupies the same amount of space regardless of the container
mcqs.explanation: A liquid’s definite volume means the amount of space it occupies does not change when transferred to containers of different shapes. Option A describes gases, while C and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which description best reflects the property that liquids have no fixed shape?

options.A: A liquid keeps the shape of the container it is in
options.B: A liquid keeps its own shape like a solid
options.C: A liquid can be compressed easily

mcqs.answer: A liquid keeps the shape of the container it is in
mcqs.explanation: Liquids adapt to the shape of their container because they lack a fixed shape. Option B describes solids, C is a property of gases, and D is unrelated to shape.
